_readme: The Still Season's arena — tower floor 2, DRUID champion.
BRIEF CHANGED BY RAHEEM after three rejected rounds of grove clearings: this is
an OVERGROWN FOREST COLOSSEUM, ruined and half-swallowed, with his pink poison
bloom spreading out from the centre and polluting everything.
THE NEW BRIEF DISSOLVES THE OLD FIGHT, which is why it is worth restating what
the first three rounds died of (kept at r1-rejected/ and r3-superseded/):
- Grey stone kept 'creeping in' and was rejected each time. A colosseum is
MADE of stone, so the model's strongest prior is now the brief instead of
the defect. Stone, masonry, ruins and columns have all LEFT the negative.
- Every round produced a receding corridor with a bright terminus — a sky, a
sunset, a mountain. Cause: 'symmetrical head-on view' + 'atmospheric depth'
+ trunks that 'flank like columns' is a one-point-perspective recipe, and a
vanishing point demands something bright at the end of it. A colosseum bowl
CLOSES ITS OWN BACKGROUND with tiered seating, so there is no terminus to
light. This was the single hardest failure and the new brief deletes it.
- 'No sky' never worked, because a negated absence asks the model to render
nothing in the highest-attention part of the frame. The rule (the arena
restatement of LEONARDO_PLAYBOOK.md's clothing lesson) is NAME THE OBJECT:
the top of the frame is now the dark canopy of trees grown through the
upper tiers, which is a thing rather than an absence.
THE CENTRE MUST STAY EMPTY, and the pollution gradient is what justifies it:
the bloom is worst at the centre and thins outward, so the composition points
at the boss without painting him. NEVER name the occupants — 'a floor where
three figures can stand' painted three tiny fighters on it once already.
NO DAIS. BossPlatform.tsx draws the platform in code. A painted dais required
every plate to land a raised surface in a narrow band at a matching camera
angle, a contract nothing enforced, so the boss's feet met it only by luck.
THE ARENA'S PINK IS DARK, MATTE AND DORMANT — never glowing. His area attack
act_season_root ('A whole season of growth arrives at once') erupts the floor
in BRIGHT magenta as a code VFX layer. If the plate already glows pink, the
attack reads as more of the floor instead of as something he just did. Dormant
stain in the plate, acute flare in code: that contrast is the whole gameplay
tell, and it is why 'glowing floor' and 'light in the ground' stay negated.
MODEL: PHOENIX, and do not switch. The CLAUDE.md note about Lucid Origin is
about flat TOP-DOWN maps; an arena is a frontal stage, which is Phoenix's
strength, and both shipped arenas are Phoenix. Pixel-cluster density is
model-specific and is the most visible cue that a tower is one building.
presetStyle 'NONE' — omitting it lets Leonardo apply a cinematic default that
pulls toward smooth matte painting. Invisible while a style ref was fighting
it; obvious the moment the ref came off.
NO styleRefFile. Both shipped plates are stone-on-stone; referencing one onto
a green brief imported its lava-web floor wholesale even at 'Low'. Set cohesion
comes instead from model, 1360x768, the shared styleHeader, lib/pixelize.py's
deterministic grid, and the composition bands below.
HARD CAPS: prompt 1500 chars, negative_prompt 1000. Both are enforced only at
submit, i.e. possibly part-way through a paid batch — harness.mjs now checks
the prompt locally first.
WHAT THE COMPOSITION OWES THE CODE:
- top-LEFT ~372x196 and top-RIGHT ~320px are HUD panels: keep them DARK
- the lower third is where the party stands: flat and LOW CONTRAST
- bottom ~8.5rem is under the command shelf; anything there is lost
- centre-middle is the boss and his platform: keep it uncluttered
SUSPENDED LEAVES ARE NOT IN THE PLATE. They failed 6/6 ('hang' implies a
hanger; 'frozen in air' is a state and Phoenix renders objects; hundreds of
3-4px objects are below the size floor). They ship as a code layer of 20-40
fixed sprites at ZERO velocity — strictly better, because everything else on
screen moves and the leaves conspicuously will not.
ROUND 4 (first colosseum pass) — concept right, two failures, one of them mine:
1. THE BLIGHT WENT TO THE PERIMETER, the exact opposite of the brief. My own
contradiction: the same paragraph called the centre 'densest and most
rotten' AND 'flat, unbroken and uncluttered'. The model resolved it by
moving the rot to the edges. The centre must stay walkable (boss +
BossPlatform), so the pollution now RADIATES OUTWARD FROM THE CENTRE IN
THE FLOOR CRACKS — thin fine veins at the origin, thickening as it climbs
and drowns the tiers. Same class of self-inflicted bug as leaving 'frozen'
in the negative while asking for leaves 'frozen in the air'. Read the
prompt back as one sentence and look for the instruction that cancels.
It also tells the story better: it has spread AWAY from him and eaten the
whole bowl, which is what 'polluting everything' should look like.
2. SKY STILL FILLS THE UPPER MIDDLE — 8 images running. A canopy described as
'meeting overhead' only ever reaches the corners, and the colosseum's far
rim becomes a horizon with sky above it. Fix: the TIERS THEMSELVES must
rise to the top edge of the frame.The structure, not the foliage, is
what closes the top. Foliage is a second layer on top of that.
styleHeader: 16-bit pixel art environment plate, retro SNES JRPG location background, hard-edged pixel clusters, limited flat palette, dithered gradients, no blur, no soft shading. Widescreen 16:9, symmetrical head-on view, empty and unoccupied. Depth comes from flat overlapping layers, not perspective: no vanishing point, no corridor, no path, no opening in the distance.

arena.line: A colossal ruined stone colosseum swallowed by forest, seen head-on from the arena floor looking up. Shattered tiers of weathered grey seating rise steeply on the left, the right and across the back, towering up and filling the frame all the way to its top edge so that no sky is visible anywhere. Huge old trees have burst up through the collapsed seating, splitting the stone into rubble, and their dark black-green canopies hang across the very top of the frame, nearly black in the upper-left and upper-right corners. Thick roots and deep moss drown the broken tiers. Fine dark magenta poison veins run outward through the cracks of the arena floor from its exact centre, spreading wider and thicker as they climb the surrounding stone until the blight smothers the far tiers, matte and unlit. The centre and lower third are flat open packed earth, uncluttered. Weathered grey stone, deep olive, umber, dull bruised magenta.

states.label: B — Root-Split Tiers (giant trunks burst the seating, forest dominant)
states.line: The interior of a vast ruined amphitheatre drowning in forest, seen head-on from its floor looking up. Colossal moss-clad tree trunks have burst upward through the tiered seating on the left and right, shattering it into rubble, and the broken tiers tower across the back and fill the frame all the way to its top edge so that no sky is visible anywhere. The trunks' dark canopies close over the very top of the frame, nearly black in the upper-left and upper-right corners. Roots pour down over the shattered benches. Fine dark magenta poison veins run outward through the cracks of the floor from its exact centre, spreading wider and thicker as they climb the stone until the blight smothers the upper tiers, matte and unlit. The centre and lower third are flat open packed earth, uncluttered. Weathered grey stone, deep olive, umber, dull bruised magenta.
states.note: Greener and more forest-dominant. Flanking verticals are trunks rather than architecture, which is closer to the shipped arenas' framing; A reads more clearly as a colosseum.
